haiku-low.q1: PRs run build plus unit tests only and never deploy. Merges to main start the whole run, including build, push, tests, and deploys.
haiku-low.q2: Both deploy the same image, registry.internal/shop-api:<sha>, built once per run and passed as IMAGE_TAG. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration test failure: retried once, and if still failing the run ends before staging. Unit test failure: no retry, and the run ends before staging.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs what it ran before, via deploy.sh rollback. That image is the previous_tag in Parameter Store at /deploy/staging/previous_tag.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers, not the commit author, may approve. Without approval within 72 hours of reaching the gate, the run expires, prod never gets it, and staging keeps the build.
haiku-low.q6: In Parameter Store at /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after the main rollout succeeds. Approver and time are in the CI run record.
haiku-low.q7: Stable stays on the old image, and the recorded tags are unchanged since the main deployment was never touched. The database keeps any canary migrations, since nothing migrates down.
haiku-low.q8: It is cancelled as superseded if it has not yet begun its prod deploy, meaning it is still waiting on sign-off, the window, or lock P.
haiku-low.q9: It waits, polling every 5 minutes, and does not lapse. Window starts are Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC only, but runs may finish after 15:00. Busy lock P makes it wait the same way.
haiku-low.q10: The pilot's 5xx share from Prometheus. The canary-check job queries once a minute for 15 minutes. Failure is any reading over 1%, or Prometheus returning nothing.
haiku-low.q11: A ping in Slack #deploys carries IMAGE_TAG, a smoke results link, and the commit list since prod's current tag. Approvers approve in the CI UI.
haiku-low.q12: Stable rollout failures get kubectl rollout undo, not deploy.sh rollback, because SSM is not yet written and rollback would go one too far back. Prod then runs canary-off.

sonnet.q1: A PR runs only build plus unit tests and reports PR status; it never deploys. A merge to main starts the full run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the same image registry.internal/shop-api:<sha>, built once per run and passed along as IMAGE_TAG. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test (it) failure: retried once. Unit test (ut) failure: no retry. Anything still failing ends the run before staging, with a fail + post to Slack.
sonnet.q4: Rollback runs: deploy.sh rollback staging, which sets staging back to previous_tag (what staging ran before). It is found via the Parameter Store tag /deploy/staging/previous_tag. Then the run fails and posts.
sonnet.q5: Only release-approvers can approve, and not the commit author. If nobody approves within 72h of reaching the gate, the run expires: prod never gets it, staging keeps the build, and an expired post goes to #deploys.
sonnet.q6: In Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. deploy.sh <env> <tag> writes both, only once the main rollout went fine. The canary (pilot) is never written.
sonnet.q7: The main/stable deployment was never touched, so the tags in the parameter store still show the old tag. The database keeps whatever the canary step migrated, because nothing migrates down, so the old image must cope with it.
sonnet.q8: When the newer run's staging smoke goes green, the older run (if it has not begun its prod deploy and is still waiting on sign-off, the window, or lock P) is cancelled as superseded, with a post to #deploys.
sonnet.q9: It waits. Outside the window (start only Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC) it polls every 5 min; an approval given Thursday evening sits until Monday 09:00 and does not lapse. If lock P is busy, it waits the same way.
sonnet.q10: The pilot's (shop-api-canary) 5xx share is measured. The canary-check job queries Prometheus once a minute for 15 minutes (after 2 pods are ready, at 10% traffic). Failure is a 5xx share over 1% even once, or Prometheus returning nothing; then canary-off is run.
sonnet.q11: A ping/approval message in Slack #deploys. It carries IMAGE_TAG, a link to the smoke results, and the commit list between prod's current_tag and this tag. People approve in the CI UI.
sonnet.q12: With kubectl rollout undo, not deploy.sh rollback, because SSM tags are not yet written at that point, so deploy.sh rollback would go one too far back. In production, canary-off follows the undo.
